summary: The MG S5 EV is the ZS EV's rear-drive replacement and is widely described by Australian reviewers as MG's most convincing model to date: a conventional, well-resolved small-to-mid electric SUV with a 453-litre boot, five-star ANCAP and pricing that sits under the Kia EV3. Reviewers agree the 62kWh car is the one to buy — the 49kWh Essence's 335km WLTP range draws consistent criticism as thin for the money — and the MY26 update cut the range to two Essence grades while adding 25kW and 25km of range to the 62 without a price rise; MG sells both at national drive-away prices and publishes no list price. Opinion splits on the chassis: CarExpert and Chasing Cars rate the handling and steering response highly, while CarsGuide finds the steering too light and the styling polarising, and Chasing Cars calls the town ride 'fairly knobbly'.
pros: Up to 10 years/250,000km warranty (7 years/unlimited km if serviced outside the MG dealer network) — matching the 7-year cover from Kia, Chery and Geely and beating BYD's 6, with more on offer if you stay with MG servicing; the battery is covered for 7 years/150,000km
MY26 Essence 62 gained 150kW/350Nm (up from 125kW/250Nm), cutting 0-100km/h from 8.6 to 7.0 seconds and lifting WLTP range from 425 to 450km, with no price rise
453L boot expanding to 1441L seats-down, plus a flat rear floor and genuine three-across rear seating — well ahead of the MG4 hatch's 350-382L and level with the Kia EV3's 460L
Five-star ANCAP (2025) with 90% adult and 86% child occupant protection
150kW DC charging gives a 30-80% top-up in about 19 minutes, and the LFP chemistry tolerates routine 100% charging
cons: Essence 49's 335km WLTP range is the range's weak point — CarExpert's verdict is that the '62 battery is far better than 49', and the step up buys 115km more range for under five thousand dollars
The 10-year warranty is conditional on every scheduled service being done inside the MG dealer network within 30 days/2,000km of each interval; miss one and cover reverts to 7 years
Firm ride that Chasing Cars calls 'fairly knobbly' around town, and CarsGuide criticises steering that is 'too light and lacks communication'
Safety assist is its weakest ANCAP score at 79%, and child presence detection was not assessed because it is not fitted to every Australian variant
MG's rolling campaigns (one thousand dollars off in July 2026, a two-thousand-dollar cashback to 31 December 2026) keep resetting the market price, which weighs on resale
